findings.summary: Names are checked with re.match, which only anchors the start, so a name like a/../../x passes and the page is written outside the directory.
Tables are rendered with the unsafehtml format, so cell text is written as raw HTML and data can inject scripts into the pages.
The index counts rows with the default headers instead of the export's headers, so with headers='firstrow' the header row is counted as a data row.

The name pattern only refuses path separators and a leading dot, so a name such as passes the check and is written unescaped into the index page's link, which injects markup; names may only hold letters, digits, _, - and . and must start with a letter or a digit.
